4fc81f300a3fbfcd.en_html: I think IDFC's strength is, above all, the quality of the people who come together. There are people with whom you can seriously discuss your future dreams and goals and the kind of person you want to be. In our usual communities, we do not often talk about those things; it feels somewhat embarrassing, and we hesitate. But at IDFC, there are friends who understand your thoughts, empathize with you, and help you. That is true of participants from both Japan and Myanmar. Honestly, I think it is fine to participate even if you cannot speak English or are not especially interested in Myanmar. Any motivation or reason for joining is fine. That was actually the case for me. (laughs) Of course, you gain the experience of international exchange, but you also find a community where you can talk about your future and always return. I think that is what makes IDFC so good.

d5a4b9522e8f04a5.en_html: There are so many. One particularly memorable moment was after the opening ceremony. The ceremony was held in a university meeting room, with the president of the University of Yangon also attending. At first, the Japanese and Myanmar participants were seated facing one another across tables. But as soon as the ceremony ended, everyone stood up, gathered at the back of the room, and started introducing themselves. At that moment, I thought, “Ah, they've come together.” People meeting for the first time and introducing themselves may, in a sense, be just one ordinary scene. Even so, it was the moment when what all of us on the organizing committee had long envisioned unfolded right before our eyes. I will never forget how moving that moment was.

d13172f33a191c4f.en_html: But at that moment, I thought something was strange. You should first think about what you want to do, for whom and where, and therefore who you want to work with. So I asked the NGO's representative directly what they wanted to do for the people living in the slum. They said, “In the future, by enabling them to receive higher education, we want children living on the streets to be able to live independently.”

When it comes to opportunities to go abroad, I do get the impression that they tend to center on Europe and North America.
